attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: No Yang-Mills estimate yet gives the Wilson hairpin quotient expansion with a uniform o(eps_delta) remainder and a correctly isolated B_delta.
steps: Start from fixed-collar reflection positivity: N_delta>=0. After diagonal trace continuity removes additive contacts, the intended normalized target block is q_delta=Nh_delta\oslash Bh_delta.
On 1^perp, J contributes nothing since z^*Jz=|sum_i z_i|^2=0; hence first-order positivity is controlled only by H.
If q_delta is positive for the same theory and r_delta=o(eps_delta), then 0<=z^*q_delta z=eps_delta z^*Hz+o(eps_delta); dividing and limiting gives z^*Hz>=0.
Contrapositively, a negative zero-sum H-form yields a negative principal OS quadratic form for small collars, so it is a valid finite falsifier.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The lemma is finite-dimensional and conditional; the actual boundary OPE coefficient H and same-theory anomaly B still must be constructed from the cutoff-removal analysis.

assumptions: Fixed-collar RG convergence is valid for all reflected pairings in the finite Wilson family.
Diagonal trace continuity and positive additive-contact compatibility eliminate additive boundary defects.
Bh_delta has nonzero entries, q_delta is Hermitian, and q_delta,ii=1.
There are eps_delta down to 0 and Hermitian H with q_delta=J+eps_delta H+r_delta and ||r_delta||/eps_delta ->0.
definitions: source object: finite collar-separated gauge-invariant Wilson observables W_i^delta with reflected OS matrices N_delta>=0 and boundary anomaly matrices B_delta from collar collapse.
target object: normalized intended continuum OS matrix q for the same Wilson observables after removing only prelocked diagonal renormalizations.
controlled interface: regulated reflection-positive Schwinger forms -> OS-positive continuum Schwinger functions via q_delta=Nh_delta\oslash Bh_delta on each finite locked Wilson block.
same-theory condition: B_delta records only collision artifacts; no new boundary observable, counterterm, or pair-dependent renormalization is inserted into the test algebra.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: Find zero-sum z with z^*Hz<0 in a realized Wilson block; then q_delta is indefinite for small delta.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Converts the first boundary OPE coefficient into a necessary finite OS positivity test on 1^perp.
candidate_lemmas.statement: If a locked finite Wilson hairpin block has normalized same-theory quotient q_delta=Nh_delta\oslash Bh_delta=J+eps_delta H+o(eps_delta), then OS positivity forces H>=0 on 1^perp. A negative zero-sum form is a finite falsifier before any log-CND claim.

control_decision.pivot_test: Pivot if H is negative on a realized Wilson zero-sum block or if no valid quotient expansion can be obtained from RG estimates.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote if the Wilson boundary OPE proves H>=0 on a dense locked core with uniform remainder, then extend to finite q_delta positivity.
control_decision.reason: The branch now has a computable infinitesimal Wilson boundary test tied directly to finite OS matrices.

dependency_updates.description: Closed-cone passage is supplemented by the tangent condition H>=0 on 1^perp for near-rank-one Wilson quotient blocks.
The locked Wilson core must include enough hairpin triples and zero-sum linear combinations to test the leading quotient kernel H.
The topology must control normalized reflected quotient expansions and remainders near the reflection plane, not only separated test forms.

falsifiers: falsifier: a boundary OPE computation gives z^*Hz<0 for some zero-sum coefficients in a three- or four-hairpin Wilson block.
falsifier: q_delta is not Hermitian after quotienting, so B_delta is not the valid same-theory anomaly or reflection was mismatched.
falsifier: additive boundary contacts have nonzero off-diagonal part despite zero diagonal, violating positive contact compatibility.
falsifier: RG convergence controls separated collars but gives no uniform o(eps_delta) remainder as supports approach t=0.
branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 215 isolates the first-order OS obstruction cleanly: near the rank-one quotient J, positivity lives on 1^perp. The valid finite test is H>=0 there; a negative zero-sum boundary OPE coefficient is an immediate same-theory falsifier.
